summary: Builds and stores a 4x4 matrix at a1 from a rotation-like basis: the input vector/quaternion a3 is normalized (inverse square root via Newton-Raphson refinement, with lazy one-time caching of the two refinement constants behind byte_8D46B0 flag bits), the normalized axis is sign-flipped with xmmword_5D8B00, and four result rows are formed from shuffle/mask operations against the incoming matrix a2 using masks xmmword_5D8B10/20/30. Stores the four rows to this+0x0/+0x10/+0x20/+0x30, choosing unaligned storel/storeh pairs when a1 is not 16-byte aligned, otherwise aligned 16-byte stores. Returns a1.

local_names.a1: output pointer to the 4-row result matrix
local_names.a2: input 4x4 matrix whose rows feed the result
local_names.a3: input vector/quaternion used to build the normalized axis
local_names.v7: masked, normalized axis (raw input when squared length is zero)
local_names.byte_8D46B0: lazy-init flags: bit0 = cache xmmword_8D4690 set, bit1 = cache xmmword_8D46A0 set

operations.description: Load the input vector/quaternion from a3 into v3.
Mask v3 with AND mask xmmword_5D8B40 and square the surviving components elementwise (v4*v4), producing the component-wise squared vector.
Horizontal sum of the squared components (add + movehl + shuffle) accumulates the squared length into v7.m128_f32[0].
If v7.m128_f32[0] (squared length) != 0.0, run the normalization block; otherwise skip it and use the raw masked vector.
Lazy one-time cache of the refinement factor: when flag bit 0 of byte_8D46B0 is clear, initialize xmmword_8D4690 from dword_8D60C0 and set the flag; subsequent calls reuse the cached xmmword_8D4690.

Lazy one-time cache of the inverse-sqrt scaling constant: when flag bit 1 of byte_8D46B0 is clear, initialize xmmword_8D46A0 from dword_8D60C4 and set the flag; subsequent calls reuse the cached xmmword_8D46A0.

Compute v11 = 1.0 / fsqrt(v7.m128_f32[0]) and apply one Newton-Raphson refinement step on the inverse square root using the two cached constants (v9.m128_f32[0] = (c1 * v11) * (c2 - (v7[0] * v11) * v11)).
Build the normalized axis: v7 = v3 * splat(refined factor), broadcasting the refined inverse-sqrt result across all four lanes.
Sign-flip the normalized axis: v13 = v7 XOR sign mask xmmword_5D8B00.
Row blending term: v14 = v7 * *a2, then v15 is the horizontal sum of v14 and v16 broadcasts that sum across all lanes.
Component extraction: v17 = v16 AND xmmword_5D8B20, v18 = v16 AND xmmword_5D8B30, and v19 = v16.m128_f32[0].
Result row 1 (stored at this+0x10): v20 = shuffle(v13, 85) * *a2 + (v16 AND xmmword_5D8B10).
Result row 2 (stored at this+0x20): v21 = shuffle(v13, 170) * *a2 + v17.
Result rows 0 and 3 (stored at this+0x0 and this+0x30): v23 = shuffle(v13, 0) * *a2 with v23.m128_f32[0] += v19, and v22 = shuffle(v13, 255) * *a2 + v18.
Branch on output alignment: if ((unsigned __int8)a1 & 0xF) != 0 use the unaligned store path, otherwise use aligned 16-byte stores.
Unaligned store path: write the four result rows to this+0x0, this+0x10, this+0x20 and this+0x30 using storel/storeh 64-bit halves.
Aligned store path: write the four __m128 result rows to this+0x0, this+0x10, this+0x20 and this+0x30.
